_comment: PROPOSED basal schedule (local clock, units U/hr). NOT applied to the live Nightscout profile. Evidence-based redesign calibrated to Loop's actual delivered basal (see REPORT.md section 11). Phased rollout recommended. Apply only via care-team / Loop workflow.

basal_step1._desc: Step 1 (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 06:48 UTC): overnight cut + midday trough + late-dinner taper.
basal_step1._night1_result: First night overshot to HIGHS overnight: mean 156, max 214, 17% >180, 0% lows. Rise tracked the 22:30 taper (118->157). Midday trough worked well (today 11:00-13:00 ran 83-119, no lows). Conclusion: evening taper too deep; deep-overnight cut was fine. See basal_step1b.

basal_step1b._desc: Step 1b (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 23:25 UTC): walk back evening/overnight cut, keep midday trough.
basal_step1b._week_result: 7-day result (Jun 14-20) vs 90d baseline. NOTE: Jun 17 was sensor day-1 (Dexcom started Jun 16 16:32) and read jumpy-low (29% lows, min 45) - excluded below. EXCL sensor day-1: OVERNIGHT 00-04 SOLVED (%<70 3.1, %<54 0.3, TIR 96.9 - better than goal). Evening fine (%<70 5.4, %<54 0.8) - the low creep was sensor noise, leave it. Dawn 04-07 lows REAL (%<70 9.7, not sensor) -> Step-1c cuts dawn. Midday 11-16 lows REAL (%<70 14.9) and rose despite basal cut => meal/bolus-driven, review lunch carb-ratio. Overall %<70 8.6 / %<54 0.4.

basal_step1c._desc: Step 1c (applied to Loop 2026-06-20 21:33 UTC): cut dawn 04:30 1.55->1.35.
basal_step1c._result: Reviewed Jul 4 (14d, incl. G6->G7 swap Jun 26; G7 warmup auto-excluded). G7 reads same level as G6 (mean 108 vs 110) so comparisons valid. Dawn FIXED (9.7->5.6% <70). Midday improved a lot (15->7.3%, real not calibration). Overnight up to 6.4% but all shallow (nadir 61-67, 0% <54) and partly G7 compression lows -> HOLD basal, don't chase. Severe lows 0.0-0.4% everywhere; excellent control. Verdict: Step-1c is a keeper; hold and watch overnight (behavioral/sensor-placement fix for compression, not basal).

basal_step2._desc: Step 2 (after ~1 week confirming step 1): trim the daytime shoulders (09:30 and merge 16:00-20:00). Merges the old 16:00/17:00 boundaries into one 1.45 afternoon block.

basal_step1d._desc: Step 1d (proposed, LOW PRIORITY - evidence weakened on review): 09:30 1.80 -> 1.45. See _evidence and _revision.
basal_step1d._evidence: 45d review (Jun 9-Jul 24), morning window. FINDING: there is effectively no breakfast - only 35% of days have a >=15g morning carb entry and median first food is 11:18am; the 4/6/8am small entries are corrections at BG~200, not meals. Early morning 04:00-09:00 is GOOD (median 108->118, modest +10 dawn rise, ~0-4% lows, ~0-3% highs) - do not touch. The problem is the LATE-MORNING FASTING SAG: on days with no food before 11:00, 14/16 drifted down, median -16 mg/dL (worst -40/-36/-69), 31% dipped <70, arriving at the first meal already low. Cause: the schedule jumps to 1.80 U/hr at 09:30 (highest daytime rate) mid-fast - apparently vestigial coverage for a breakfast no longer eaten. Loop fights it: hour 10 delivers 1.24 vs 1.80 scheduled, 25% suspended (hr 11: 0.81 vs 1.25, 29% suspended). Morning is the cleanest window for analysis (~0.2 Afrezza-like drops/wk, few fake carbs), so this is fasting-grade evidence.
basal_step1d._revision: REVISED after learning the subject is SLEEPING IN (summer). The 09:00-11:30 window is therefore still SLEEP, not a daytime fast, so the same G7 compression that inflates overnight lows also applies here (lying on the sensor). Re-running with compression episodes excluded: median fasting drift shrinks from -16 to -9 mg/dL (11/12 days still fall, so direction is robust but magnitude halved), and %<70 in 09:00-11:30 falls to ~0-4% (the '31% dipped <70' was largely artifact). The 'Loop is suspending 25%' signal is also partly circular - compression lows cause Loop to suspend. Landing at ~96-101 before the first meal is acceptable. VERDICT: the 09:30 bump is still anomalous but the case for changing it is weak and the pattern is SEASONAL (will shift when school resumes). Prefer to hold, or use a Loop Override on sleep-in days rather than editing the permanent schedule.

first_meal_review_2026_07_24._desc: First-meal-of-day analysis (the real 'breakfast', ~12:18 due to summer sleep-in). The best-supported meal-side finding to date, because the morning window is comparatively free of unlogged Afrezza (~0.2/wk) and fake carbs (>=25g filter).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._finding: Strongly asymmetric: 22% of first meals dip <70 within 4h vs only 2% peaking >180, with median peak just 135. The dose is a touch strong for the starting point - he arrives at ~89 already drifting down, then boluses at an effective CR of 5.7 (stronger than the profile's 6).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._option: Weaken the first-meal carb ratio in the window he actually eats (currently ~10:00-15:00): CR 6 -> 7. A 50g meal would take ~7.1U instead of ~8.3U (~1.2U less, ~60 mg/dL at ISF 53). Expected: most of the 22% lows resolve; peak rises from ~135 toward ~150-160, still well under 180. SEASONAL CAVEAT: the window is tied to the summer sleep-in and will need revisiting when the schedule shifts.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._caution: Single-variable discipline: do NOT combine with a basal change. ISF stays unvalidated (corrections are mostly invisible Afrezza/fake-carb).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._meal_taxonomy: CORRECTED: the first meal of the day is always BREAKFAST regardless of clock time (subject sleeps in; summer). Sometimes there is no lunch, or only a snack. Analysis is therefore by meal ORDINAL, not clock hour. Breakfast n=45 median 12:15 (IQR 11:48-12:54); mid-meal/snack n=23 median 15:38; dinner n=41 median 19:27.

breakfast.read: over-insulinized relative to need: 22% low vs 4% high, peak only 133

mid_meal_snack.read: chaotic both directions; small n and sits in the dinner-time Afrezza window - DO NOT TUNE

dinner.read: balanced 17/17 - leave alone; already effectively dosed weaker than breakfast

first_meal_review_2026_07_24._two_wave_finding: KEY. Post-breakfast median trajectory shows TWO low waves, not one: (a) an EARLY dip at 30-90min (BG 89 -> 84 at 30min; 16% <70 at 60min) - the prebolus acting before the food, from an already-low start; and (b) a LATE wave at 240-270min (13-16% <70) - the insulin tail. Median time from breakfast to first <70 is 80 min (IQR 60-230), so the EARLY dip dominates. The meal does not peak until ~180min and only reaches 136. Interpretation: this is primarily a STARTING-BG + PREBOLUS-TIMING problem, not purely carb ratio.
_options_ranked: 1. BEHAVIORAL (zero settings risk, targets the dominant 30-90min dip): when pre-breakfast BG is <90 and flat/falling, skip or shorten the prebolus - bolus at first bite instead.

2. BASAL (passive, no behavior change needed): Step-1d 09:30 1.80 -> 1.45 now has a better rationale - not the -9 drift itself, but arriving at breakfast nearer 98-100 instead of 89 gives the prebolus dip headroom before it crosses 70.
3. CARB RATIO (targets the late 240-270min wave): breakfast-window CR 6 -> 6.5 (~8%, standard increment). CR 7 is the more decisive test given peak is only 133, but 6.5 is the by-the-book first step.
Do ONE at a time. Dinner and mid-meal should not be changed.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._seasonal: All of this is tied to the summer sleep-in: breakfast is currently ~12:15. When school resumes, breakfast moves earlier and any time-windowed CR segment (and the 09:30 basal rationale) must be revisited.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._CORRECTION: METHODOLOGICAL ERROR in the first pass, now fixed. Peaks were measured in a 2.5h window, but breakfast does not peak until ~3h, so the peak was TRUNCATED and highs under-reported. Corrected 5h window (n=45): median peak 165 (not 133), 29% exceed 180 (not 4%), 51% dip below 70, and 16% do BOTH within the same meal; only 36% are clean. CONCLUSION REVERSED: breakfast swings both ways - it is NOT simply over-insulinized, so weakening the carb ratio is the WRONG fix (it would worsen the 29% highs). The problem is shape/timing, not dose magnitude.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._behavioral_rule_test: The proposed rule 'pre-BG <95 and flat/falling -> skip prebolus' does NOT discriminate: risky group 35% dip <70 within 2h vs 32% for all others (n=17 vs 28). Trend direction ran backwards from expectation (falling 22% early-dip vs flat 50%, rising 39%) - noise at this n. The ONLY surviving signal is the starting level: pre-BG <80 -> 60% dip <70 (n=10) vs 22-38% for all higher bands.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._recommendation_2026_07: HOLD ALL SETTINGS. (1) The data cannot support a confident breakfast change - both-ways swing, no clean threshold. (2) The pattern is tied to the summer sleep-in (12:15 breakfast) and is about to be erased by travel and then a college dorm. (3) A change made now would be evaluated during travel, the noisiest possible baseline. Keep Step-1c (holding well: TIR 93%, GMI 5.9%). Carry ONE portable, BG-triggered rule that survives time zones and a shifting class schedule: do not take a full meal bolus starting under 80 - eat the first bites first or bring BG up before dosing. Re-assess 2-3 weeks into the dorm once a routine exists. NOTE: user correctly ruled out a time-of-day basal segment for the morning - first class varies by day, so a clock-based fix cannot work.

pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._desc: POD-CYCLE (3-day Omnipod) EFFECT - user hypothesis, confirmed. Largest single systematic driver of variability found to date, and the only intervention that is schedule-independent (anchored to pod changes, not the clock).
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._data: 45d, 19 site changes, median pod life 2.5d (two <1d = likely failures). Bolus insulin is FLAT across pod days (43.1/43.8/43.8 U/day) so this is an ABSORPTION effect, not a dosing difference.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._robustness: Gradient holds in EVERY time-of-day window after excluding G7 compression (%<70 day1/2/3): night 3.7/0.2/0.6, morning 6.4/4.2/1.4, afternoon 10.4/6.8/4.0, evening 9.3/5.0/3.9. Mean glucose rises monotonically with pod age in every window. Not a time-of-day artifact - pod changes cluster in the afternoon/evening but the effect survives matching on time of day.

_breakfast_by_pod_day.note: Explains the previously confusing 'breakfast swings both ways' result: the highs are concentrated on pod day 3 (peak +37 vs day 1, 55% >180), the lows on day 1. Two distinct problems that averaged into one. Low side is noisier at this n (44/69/36) - the peak/high gradient is the clean signal.

pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._direction: Fresh site absorbs BETTER (more insulin action -> lows on day 1); absorption degrades with pod age (less action -> highs on day 3). Note this is the OPPOSITE of what a naive 'day 1 is erratic' expectation predicts, and the magnitude (mean 105 -> 118, lows 7.4% -> 2.5%) is comparable to the entire basal retune.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._why_it_fits_the_constraints: Anchored to pod changes (~every 2.5d), NOT the clock. Survives travel, time zones, a college dorm, and a class schedule that differs by day - precisely where a time-of-day basal segment fails.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._option: A pod-day-aware Loop Override pair: a gentler-insulin override for roughly the first 12-24h after a pod change (to cut the day-1 lows) and/or a stronger one for the last ~12h before a change (to cut the day-3 highs). Loop overrides scale basal/ISF/CR together and can be time-limited. MAGNITUDE NOT ESTABLISHED HERE - start conservative (~5-10%) and set with the care team; do not derive the percentage from these aggregates.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._caveats: Breakfast-by-pod-day cells are small (n=11-16). The overall gradient is robust (n=2731-4999/day). Two sub-1-day pod gaps (failures) were left in. Site-change events are user-logged; an unlogged change would blur the boundaries.
